title: Chapter 2 – Cost Concepts & Value Chain (Objectives)
notes: Identify the key attributes of service, merchandising and manufacturing companies
Identify and describe the elements of the value chain
Distinguish between direct and indirect costs
Distinguish between inventoriable product costs and period costs and identify their proper treatment for merchandising and manufacturing firms
Prepare the financial statements for service, merchandising and manufacturing companies
Identify relevant and irrelevant costs for decision making
Classify costs as fixed or variable and calculate total and average costs at different levels of activity (volume)

flashcards.front: Service vs Merchandising vs Manufacturing: key difference?
flashcards.back: Service sells intangible services; Merchandising buys and resells products; Manufacturing converts raw materials into finished goods.
Raw Materials, Work in Process (WIP), and Finished Goods.
Merchandising: one inventory (Merchandise Inventory). Manufacturing: RM, WIP, FG.

flashcards.front: What are the elements of the value chain?
flashcards.back: R&D, Design, Production/Purchases, Marketing, Distribution, Customer Service.

flashcards.front: Which value-chain elements are inventoriable in manufacturing?
flashcards.back: Production only (DM, DL, MOH) are product (inventoriable) costs; others are period costs.
Costs traced to a cost object (e.g., steel in a car).
Costs not conveniently traced; allocated (e.g., factory utilities).
Product costs attach to units (DM, DL, MOH) and are expensed as COGS when sold; Period costs (selling/admin) expensed in period.
Purchase cost + freight-in + import duties (less discounts).
Direct Materials + Direct Labor + Manufacturing Overhead.

flashcards.front: Basic structure: Service company income statement?
flashcards.back: Revenues – Operating expenses = Operating income (no COGS).
Sales – COGS (from Merchandise Inventory) = Gross profit; minus operating expenses.

flashcards.front: Manufacturer COGM/COGS: where do product costs flow?
flashcards.back: RM → WIP (add DL, MOH) → FG → COGS when sold.
Relevant: future costs that differ among alternatives; Irrelevant: sunk or same across choices.
Benefit forgone by choosing one alternative over another.
Fixed: total constant in relevant range; Variable: total changes in proportion to volume.
Average cost = Total cost ÷ units; Total cost = Fixed + Variable.
